verses.zh: 万军之耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: Then the message of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] came to me as follows:
notes: There is a remarkable concentration of this name of God in this section of Zechariah, 18 times in this chapter out of 53 in the book. It emphasizes the Lord’s sovereignty in contrast to the human impossibility of accomplishing what lies ahead.
verses.commentary: 8:1 This is a literary marker introducing a new stage of the discussion. See note at Zech. 7:1.

verses.zh: 「万军之耶和华如此说：我为锡安心里极其火热，我为她火热，向她的仇敌发烈怒。
verses.en: “The Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘I am very much concerned for Zion; indeed, I am so concerned for her that my rage will fall on those who hurt her.’
verses.commentary:
8:2 "the Lord of hosts" This was a common post-exilic title.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "I am exceedingly jealous" See full notes at Zech. 1:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY/ZEAL

▣ "Zion" This is one of the seven hills of Jerusalem, but it came to stand for the entire city,
including Mount Moriah on which the temple stood. See note at Zech. 1:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣

NASB, NRSV
"with great wrath"

NKJV
"with great fervor"

TEV
"made me angry"

NJB
"furious jealousy"

REB, JPSOA
"fiercely jealous"

LXX
"with great jealousy"

Peshitta
"with great zeal"

The Hebrew root (BDB 404) means "to be hot." The implication here is YHWH's passion
(the Piel stem means "to conceive"). This term is often used by the seventh century prophets
(i.e., Jeremiah and Ezekiel, note specifically Ezek. 36:6-7). The interpretive question is how to
understand "wrath." Is it meant to refer

- to YHWH's hot passion for His people?

- to His anger at those nations He chose to discipline His people?

I believe the Hebrew phrase, "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, with great wrath, I
am jealous" best fits option #2 (cf. NIV, REB). This is not the same Hebrew word as Zech. 7:12 (BDB 893).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：我现在回到锡安，要住在耶路撒冷中。耶路撒冷必称为诚实的城，万军之耶和华的山必称为圣山。
verses.en: The Lord says, ‘I have returned to Zion and will live within Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] Now Jerusalem will be called “truthful city,” “mountain of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,” “holy mountain.”’
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
8:3 "I will return to Zion" YHWH had left the temple in Jerusalem (cf. Ezekiel 10) because of the
Jews' idolatry (cf. Ezekiel 8), before the city was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar II (cf. Ezekiel 9). YHWH Himself went
to be with the Jews in exile (cf. Ezekiel 1). The faithful ones in exile would be the new people of God.

His return (BDB 996, KB 1427; Qal PERFECT) was the confirmation that
He had forgiven His people and renewed His covenant with them.

▣ "will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem" There is no greater blessing than the personal presence
of YHWH with His people (e.g., Exod. 25:8; Lev. 26:11-12; Num. 5:3; 35:23; Deut. 23:14; Isa. 7:14, "Immanuel"). The sacrificial
system and temple were the hope of sinful people who YHWH would forgive (cf. Exod. 29:45).

Notice these two phrases are parallel with (both Qal PERFECTS) each
other, as are the next two phrases in Zech. 8:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"the City of Truth"

NRSV, TEV
"the faithful city"

NJB
"the Faithful City"

REB, JPSOA
"the City of Faithfulness"

LXX
"a city that is true"

This could also be translated "city of faithfulness." The faithful God had
returned to the faithless descendants of Abraham.

In Isa. 1:21-23 Jerusalem is sarcastically called "the faithful city," yet in Isa. 1:24-26
YHWH the Faithful will change her and forgive her so that she would truly be "the faithful city"
(cf. Zech. 8:2b) again.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO CITIES
IN ISAIAH

▣ "the mountain of the Lord" This refers to the temple area or
Mt. Moriah ("YHWH provides"). This is the place where:

- Melchizedek was anointed priest/king, Genesis 14

- Abraham was to offer Isaac, Genesis 22

- David offered a sacrifice to stop God's judgment, 1 Chr. 21:9-30

- Solomon built the temple, 2 Chr. 3:1

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH

▣ "the Holy Mountain" It is holy because YHWH's presence is there. His presence must be
reflected in His people (cf. Deut. 28:9). They must be different; they must be like Him (e.g., Lev. 19:2
[1 Pet. 1:16]; Matt. 5:48). For a good discussion of "holy," see Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT.

See a good note on the biblical use of "mountain" in NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 1051-1054.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：将来必有年老的男女坐在耶路撒冷街上，因为年纪老迈就手拿拐杖。
verses.en: Moreover, the Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘Old men and women will once more live in the plazas of Jerusalem, each one leaning on a cane because of advanced age.
verses.commentary:
8:4 "old men and old women" Most of the elderly died because of the exile and those who grew old
in Babylon could not easily return, therefore, elderly people in the land was a sign of lengthy prosperity
(cf. Deut. 28:3) or the New Age (cf. Isa. 65:20).

verses.zh: 城中街上必满有男孩女孩玩耍。
verses.en: And the streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing.[NOTE:1]
notes: The references to longevity and to children living and playing in peace are eschatological in tone. Elsewhere the millennial kingdom is characterized in a similar manner (cf. Isa 65:20; Jer 31:12-13).
verses.commentary:
8:5 "boys and girls playing" This was a sign of God's blessing (cf. Deut. 28:4) and normal social
life. This shows the reversal of YHWH's curses (i.e., the fall of Jerusalem, cf. Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29) and His
restored presence and blessing (i.e., Isa. 65:17-23; Jer. 31:12-13)!

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：到那日，这事在余剩的民眼中看为希奇，在我眼中也看为希奇吗？这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: And,’ says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, ‘though such a thing may seem to be difficult in the opinion of the small community of those days, will it also appear difficult to me?’ asks the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
verses.commentary:
8:6 "If it is too difficult" The Jewish people had become accustomed to captivity and judgment so
these promises overwhelmed them! The term "difficult" (BDB 810, Niphal IMPERFECT) also
means "wonderful." See note at Dan. 8:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

▣ "the remnant of this people" The Hebrew term "remnant" (BDB 984) basically means
"the remainder," "what is left," "the residue." In the prophets it takes on a special meaning, "the
faithful remnant," which refers to the few descendants of Abraham who believed, trusted, and worshiped
YHWH. It is these He would restore (cf. Isa. 37:4,32; 46:3; Jer. 23:3; 31:7; Micah 2:12; 5:7,8; 7:18;
Zeph. 2:7,9; Ezra 9:14; Zech. 8:6,11,12). The difficulty about this term is the time factor. Does it
refer to

- the post-exilic period (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: POST EXILIC CHART)

- the end-time (notice the phrase in Zech. 8:6, "in those days")

This may be an example of multiple fulfillment prophecy.

SEE SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "will it also be too difficult in My sight" There is a faith connection between YHWH's acts
and the faith of His people. However, even if YHWH's people do not have faith, He still acts. He is
committed to sinful humanity's redemption (cf. Zech. 8:7-8; Ezek. 36:22-38).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：我要从东方从西方救回我的民。
verses.en: “The Lord of Heaven’s Armies asserts, ‘I am about to save my people from the lands of the east and the west.
verses.commentary:
8:7 "save" The Hebrew VERB "save" (BDB 446, KB 448 Hiphil
PARTICIPLE, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION
(OT Term) is used in several senses.

- Hiphil = "to deliver" (cf. Zech. 9:9; Jer. 30:7-11; 31:7-8) or "to give victory"
(e.g., Isa. 59:16; 63:5)

- Niphal = "to be liberated," "to be saved," or "to be victorious"

It is used of the activity of YHWH on behalf of His people (cf. Zech. 8:7,13; 9:16; 10:6; 12:7).
He delivers those who trust Him (e.g., Zech. 8:6; Ps. 37:40; 86:2).

Just a note to acknowledge that modern scholarship is still uncertain about the origin or
root meaning of this term. It has been assumed that it is from an Arabic root meaning "to be wide or
spacious," but there is not a consensus.

In this context YHWH is promising to deliver His people from exile and restore them to
the Promised Land. However, the apocalyptic nature of the book projects this promise into the future as
well as the present. It surely refers to the return to Jerusalem in 538 B.C. (Cyrus' decree),
but since "the nations" (e.g., Zech. 2:11; 8:20-23) are included and the concept of Messiah is revealed
and expanded in chapters 9-14, then this must also have an eschatological focus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "east. . .west" These compass directions are used in the universal sense as in Ps. 50:1;
113:3; Isa. 59:19; Mal. 1:11.

verses.zh: 我要领他们来，使他们住在耶路撒冷中。他们要作我的子民，我要作他们的　神，都凭诚实和公义。」
verses.en: And I will bring them to settle within Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God,[NOTE:1] in truth and righteousness.’
notes: The affirmation They will be my people, and I will be their God speaks of covenant renewal, a restoration of the unbroken fellowship the Lord desired to have with his people but which their disloyalty had shattered. In the eschaton God and Israel will be in covenant union once again (cf. Jer 31:33).
verses.commentary:
8:8 "My people and I will be their God" This is covenant language (e.g., Lev. 26:12; Deut. 4:20;
18:2; 29:12-13; Jer. 31:33; 32:38; Hosea 2:23) and clearly shows that the covenant is restored.

"God" is Elohim; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "truth" This Hebrew word (BDB 54) means "firmness," "faithfulness," or "truth." Originally it
referred to a stable stance and then came to be used as imagery for that which is trustworthy, faithful or
reliable. This then becomes a description of YHWH (e.g., Ps. 71:22; 117:2; 146:6; Isa. 38:18-19;
Neh. 9:33). Faithless, fallen humanity's only hope is in the unchanging, faithful mercy of God!

This term is used in Zechariah 8 several times (cf. Zech. 8:3,8,16 [twice], 19) in the sense
of "truth." In Zech. 7:9 and 8:16 it refers to a true or faithful testimony in court. Zechairah 8:16 and
19 are parallel and speak of the truthful and trustworthy relationship between covenant partners in society.
Truth has a corporate societal focus. Truth is relational as well as propositional!

For a good discussion of this Hebrew word in all its forms see New International
Dictionary of Old Testament Theology and Exegesis, vol. 1, pp. 427-433.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：「当建造万军之耶和华的殿，立根基之日的先知所说的话，现在你们听见，应当手里强壮。
verses.en: “The Lord of Heaven’s Armies also says, ‘Gather strength, you who are listening to these words today from the mouths of the prophets who were there at the founding of the house of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,[NOTE:1] so that the temple might be built.
notes: These prophets who were there at the founding of the house of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies included at least Haggai and Zechariah, and perhaps others. The founding referred to here is not the initial laying of the temple’s foundations in 536 b.c. (Ezra 3:8) but the resumption of work two years before the time of the present narrative (i.e., in 520 b.c.), as vv. 10-12 make clear.
verses.commentary:
8:9 "Let your hands be strong" This is a Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 304, KB 302) used
in a JUSSIVE sense. Notice that this idiomatic phrase begins and concludes (cf. Zech. 8:13)
this paragraph. This phrase shows the human side of the covenant relationship. This same kind of encouragement to
faithful trust and steadfastness is found in Josh. 1:6-9; 1 Chr. 22:13; Isa. 35:4.

This may be an allusion to Haggai 2:4, who prophesied just before Zechariah. Both of them
addressed the same issue—the rebuilding of the temple needs to be finished. Throughout Israel's
history YHWH has encouraged His leaders and people to be strong and courageous and not to fear (e.g., Josh. 1:6-9;
1 Chr. 22:13; Isa. 35:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

verses.zh: 那日以先，人得不着雇价，牲畜也是如此；且因敌人的缘故，出入之人不得平安，乃因我使众人互相攻击。
verses.en: Before that time there was no compensation for man or animal, nor was there any relief from adversity for those who came and went, because I had pitted everybody—each one—against everyone else.
verses.commentary:
8:10 This is a summary of what life in Palestine was like ("before those days") between the fall of
Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II (586 B.C.) and the return ("but now" of Zech. 8:11) to Jerusalem
decreed by Cyrus II (538 B.C.).

The phrase "I set all men one against another" is the exact opposite of Zech. 8:3-8. YHWH's
presence or absence can be noted by how people treat each other (cf. Zech. 7:8-14). We reap what we sow
(cf. Gal. 6:7; and full list of all texts dealing with this subject). This is a recurrent theme in both the Old and New
Testaments. Israel reaped the bounty of the presence and forgiveness of God (cf. Zech. 8:11-12).

Notice that YHWH takes personal responsibility for Israel and Judah's exile (cf. Zech. 8:14;
7:14). He allowed foreign nations to defeat His people (cf. Isa. 10:5; Jer. 13:9; 51:20). This judgment was the
necessary discipline to bring about a renewed covenant and people. His judgment was a sign of His love (i.e., parental discipline).

verses.zh: 但如今，我待这余剩的民必不像从前。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: But I will be different now to this remnant of my people from the way I was in those days,’ says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies,
verses.commentary:
8:11 "the remnant" See note at Zech. 8:6 and
SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses).

verses.zh: 因为他们必平安撒种，葡萄树必结果子，地土必有出产，天也必降甘露。我要使这余剩的民享受这一切的福。
verses.en: ‘for there will be a peaceful time of sowing, the vine will produce its fruit, and the ground its yield, and the skies[NOTE:1] will rain down dew. Then I will allow the remnant of my people to possess all these things.
notes: Or “the heavens” (so KJV, NAB, NIV). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “skies” depending on the context.
verses.commentary: 8:12 This reflects the covenant blessings of Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29 (cf. Hag. 2:19).

verses.zh: 犹大家和以色列家啊，你们从前在列国中怎样成为可咒诅的；照样，我要拯救你们，使人称你们为有福的（或译：使你们叫人得福）。你们不要惧怕，手要强壮。
verses.en: And it will come about that just as you, both Judah and Israel, were a curse to the nations, so I will save you and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid! Instead, be strong.’
verses.commentary:
8:13 This is a very important verse because it shows the intended purpose of Israel. YHWH called
Abraham to call a world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6). His special relationship and blessing to the
descendants of Abraham was meant to attract the notice of the rest of the sons of Adam. The nationalism of
Genesis 10-11 is reflected in v. 10c. However, the Jewish people were not faithful to the covenant. Their
lives did not reflect the holiness of YHWH, but the fallenness of Genesis 3. Those who were meant to be a
light became a deterrent (cf. Ezek. 36:18-23). YHWH had to first change His own people's hearts and minds.
They could not perform His covenant requirements. Therefore, a new covenant was required; one based on
YHWH's character and provision (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:24-36). With this new covenant His people can
become their intended "blessing" to a lost world.

The "curse" of Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29 has been removed through the
Messiah. The tragedy is that Israel did not recognize this new opportunity to fulfill her worldwide
missionary mandate. She turned inward into exclusivism and pride instead of outward. YHWH's heart for "the
nations" was not her heart. Monotheism and the unity of mankind (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) demands a universal
people! Israel was a means to that end, not that end! The new age of righteousness depicted in Isaiah 55-66
was not fulfilled in the post-exilic return, but it will be in the Messianic Kingdom.

PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

▣ "Do not fear; let your hands be strong" These are both Qal IMPERFECTS
used in a JUSSIVE sense (cf. Zech. 8:9,15). This is a recurrent admonition. See note at v. 9.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：「你们列祖惹我发怒的时候，我怎样定意降祸，并不后悔。
verses.en: “For the Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘As I had planned to hurt[NOTE:1] you when your fathers made me angry,’ says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, ‘and I was not sorry,
notes: The verb זָמַם (zamam) usually means “to plot to do evil,” but with a divine subject (as here), and in light of v. 15 where it means to plan good, the meaning here has to be the implementation of discipline (cf. NCV, CEV “punish”). God may bring hurt but its purpose is redemptive and/or pedagogical.
verses.commentary:
8:14 "I purposed" The VERB (BDB 273, KB 273, Qal PERFECT) is used
in both v. 14 and v. 15.

- as YHWH "purposed" to judge His people because of their repeated covenant violations in the exiles of Assyria and Babylon

- now YHWH "purposed" to forgive and bless the returning exiled Jews (cf. v. 11)

YHWH is in control of history (i.e., Dan. 2:21). Covenant violations require a divine response (i.e., Lev. 26; Deut. 28). However,
repentance and faithfulness bring divine blessing (i.e., "the two ways," cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Proverbs 1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "I have not relented" The Hebrew VERB (BDB 636, KB 688), in its Niphal
PERFECT stem originally referred to taking a deep breath. It came to refer to relief or sorrow (see
a good brief word study in Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 87-93). YHWH was patient with His people.
He relented of the punishment that they deserved (cf. Amos 7:3,6), but there was a limit to His relenting
(cf. Jer. 15:8). There came a time when YHWH disciplined His people and He did not relent (cf. Zech. 8:14;
Ezek. 24:14), but He wanted to (cf. Jer. 26:3,13; Hosea 11:8).

This anthropomorphic word "relented" or "repented" shocks us because we think of God as unchangeable.
It is surely true that His character and commitment to redemption are unchangeable, however, if God is unchangeable in
all ways, why do we pray? Intercessory prayer is based on the belief that supplication can change God's
dealings with humans, both individually and corporately. There is a true personal relationship between God
and believers.

God's word is sure, both positively and negatively (e.g., Jer. 4:28; Ezek. 24:14; Gal. 6:7).
God's faithless people finally reaped the consequences of their acts (cf. Zech. 7:9-14). God allowed exile
to make restoration a possibility (cf. Zech. 8:15). God wants a people who reflect His character
(cf. Zech. 8:8, 16-17; 7:9-10) so that the nations can know Him and trust Him!

TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

verses.zh: 现在我照样定意施恩与耶路撒冷和犹大家，你们不要惧怕。
verses.en: so, to the contrary, I have planned in these days to do good to Jerusalem and Judah—do not fear!
verses.commentary:
8:15 Judgment is YHWH's last resort. He wants to bless (e.g., Hosea 11:8) to fulfill His larger
redemptive purposes (i.e., to restore all humans made in His image into fellowship with their Creator).

verses.zh: 你们所当行的是这样：各人与邻舍说话诚实，在城门口按至理判断，使人和睦。
verses.en: These are the things you must do: Speak the truth, each of you, to one another. Practice true and righteous judgment in your courts.[NOTE:1]
notes: For a similar reference to true and righteous judgment see Mic 6:8.
verses.commentary:
8:16-17 "These are the things which you should do" These verses reflect Zech. 7:9-10 and 8:8, but they
truly reflect the Mosaic legislation. It was very clear to these Jewish people what
YHWH's two-pronged will for them was among each other and foreigners (i.e. two positive commands in Zech. 8:16 and two
negative commands in 8:17).

This ethical aspect to biblical faith is needed in a day like theirs and ours when faith in
God is limited to:

- initial decision (ticket to heaven)

- emotional moment

- selected times and places

- rituals/liturgy

These things are good, but unless they issue in a daily, moral lifestyle they are false hopes
(cf. Matthew 7; John 15; 2 Peter 2). The goal of biblical faith is not only heaven when we die, but
Christlikeness now (cf. Matt. 5:48; Rom. 8:28-30; 1 Cor. 3:18; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:6; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13; 4:3;
5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15). Anything less is biblically suspect! Western Christianity is characterized by "what is in it for me?"
but true biblical faith is meant to serve and reflect God!

▣ "gates" This was the place of judicial acts and social events. For a good discussion of Israel's
judicial system, see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 152-155.

verses.zh: 谁都不可心里谋害邻舍，也不可喜爱起假誓，因为这些事都为我所恨恶。这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: Do not plan evil in your hearts against one another. Do not favor a false oath—these are all things that I hate,’ says the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
8:17 The first two negated VERBS are Qal IMPERFECTS used in a
JUSSIVE sense. YHWH hates premeditated schemes (i.e., Ps. 36:4; Prov. 3:29; 12:2; 14:22; Jer. 4:14;
Micah 2:1; Zech. 7:10)!

▣ "all these are what I hate" Both

- "hate" (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal PERFECT, cf. Prov. 6:16-19)

- "love" (BDB 12, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense and the
Qal IMPERATIVE, Zech. 8:19)

are human emotions applied to God (anthropomorphism, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD
DESCRIBED AS HUMAN)

God is surely personal and thereby has feelings and emotions, but His holy,
gracious, unchanging character controls the mood swings experienced by fallen humans. These words are
analogous, not definitive!

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The message of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies came to me as follows:

verses.zh: 「万军之耶和华如此说：四月、五月禁食的日子，七月、十月禁食的日子，必变为犹大家欢喜快乐的日子和欢乐的节期；所以你们要喜爱诚实与和平。」
verses.en: “The Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘The fast of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth[NOTE:1] months will become joyful and happy, pleasant feasts for the house of Judah; so love truth and peace.’
notes: The fasts of the fifth and seventh months, mentioned previously (7:5), are listed here along with the observances of the fourth and tenth months. The latter commemorated the siege of Jerusalem by the Babylonians on January 15, 588 b.c. (2 Kgs 25:1), and the former the breach of the city walls on or about July 18, 586 b.c. (Jer 39:2-5).
verses.commentary:
8:19 This literary unit begins in Zech. 7:1 with a question about the need to continue certain
fast days related to the Babylonian exile. After discussing the reason for the exile and the hope of
restoration, Zechariah returns to the question about specific fast days.

▣ "The fast of the fourth" This was a fast in memory of Jerusalem's walls being breached
(cf. Jer. 39:2; 2 Kgs. 25:3).

▣ "the fast of the fifth" This was a fast in memory of the destruction of the temple
(cf. 2 Kgs. 25:8).

▣ "the fast of the seventh" This was a fast in memory of Gedaliah's death (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:25).

▣ "the fast of the tenth" This was a fast in memory of the beginning of Nebuchadnezzar II's siege
of Jerusalem (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:1-2; Jer. 39:1).

▣ "will become joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts" There will be no more fasts! Israel's mourning
will be changed to joy, her captivity into deliverance (cf. Jer. 31:10-14). Isaiah 65 combines a renewed
Jerusalem with the New Age!

▣ "so love truth and peace" This is a summary statement of how repentant, restored, faithful followers
should live (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL). Love is more than an emotion! It is an action
(i.e., Jesus' two great commandments).

The phrase is similar to the Shema of Deut. 6:4-6. Eternal life has observable characteristics.

"Truth" is from the root (BDB 52, KB 63) which denotes faithfulness; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS).

"Peace" is both an attitude toward life and others as well as a wish that all can participate in it. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom).

True faith is lived out among one's peers, community, and kin!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：「将来必有列国的人和多城的居民来到。
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘It will someday come to pass that people—residents of many cities—will come.
verses.commentary:
8:20-21 As some came (possibly from Bethel (cf. Zech. 7:2) to seek the favor of the Lord, so now other
cities of Judah come to Jerusalem and the new temple to seek YHWH's blessing.

verses.zh: 这城的居民必到那城，说：『我们要快去恳求耶和华的恩，寻求万军之耶和华；我也要去。』
verses.en: The inhabitants of one will go to another and say, “Let’s go up at once to ask the favor of the Lord, to seek the Lord of Heaven’s Armies. Indeed, I’ll go with you.”’
verses.commentary:
8:21 "to seek the Lord" There are two parallel phrases:

- "to entreat the favor of" ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 318 II,
KB 316

- "to seek" ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 134, KB 152

The VERB "seek" (BDB 134, KB 152, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
is used twice in vv. 21-22. It is a powerful VERB of action. Seeking YHWH implies a desire to know Him
and follow Him. It denotes a sense of spiritual need as well as YHWH's desire to be found by humans made in His image and likeness.

- seek the face of YHWH ‒ 1 Sam. 21:1

- seek HIs face ‒ Ps. 105:4

- seek YHWH ‒ Exod. 33:7; Deut. 4:29; 1 Chr. 16:10; 2 Chr. 11:16; Prov. 28:5; Isa. 51:1; Jer. 50:4;
Hosea 3:5; 5:6; Zeph. 1:6; 2:3

- seek Me ‒ 2 Chr. 15:2,4; Ps. 78:34; Isa. 45:19,22; 55:6; Jer. 29:13

Notice in this context all humans may come and worship YHWH!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "I will also go" This is an emphatic statement of intent (two COHORTATIVE
forms of "go," cf. Zech. 8:23). There is an urgency to Zech. 8:21.

verses.zh: 必有列邦的人和强国的民来到耶路撒冷寻求万军之耶和华，恳求耶和华的恩。
verses.en: Many peoples and powerful nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the Lord of Heaven’s Armies and to ask his favor.
verses.commentary:
8:22 "So many peoples and mighty nations will come" The Hebrew ADJECTIVE "mighty"
(BDB 783) can mean "numerous" (cf. Ps. 35:18; Prov. 7:26; Isa. 53:12; Amos 5:12). If so, then "many peoples"
is parallel to "numerous nations."

As other Jews come so now the initial purpose of YHWH is fulfilled when "many peoples and
mighty nations" come to Him (i.e., 1 Kgs. 8:43,60). This universal aspect in Zechariah (cf. Zech. 2:11) is surprising in light of

- Zech. 1:15,21

- the racial tone of Haggai

- the problems faced by Nehemiah (cf. Neh. 4:6)

Zechariah is looking beyond the immediate (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 56:7; 66:18-24; Micah 4:1-3). He is
looking to the days of "the wounded shepherd" (cf. Zechariah, chapters 12-13)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：在那些日子，必有十个人从列国诸族（原文是方言）中出来，拉住一个犹大人的衣襟，说：『我们要与你们同去，因为我们听见　神与你们同在了。』」
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies says, ‘In those days 10 people from all languages and nations will grasp hold of—indeed, grab—the robe of one Jew and say, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.”’”[NOTE:1]
notes: This scene of universal and overwhelming attraction of the nations to Israel’s God finds initial fulfillment in the establishment of the church (Acts 2:5-11) but ultimate completion in the messianic age (Isa 45:14, 24; 60:14; Zech 14:16-21).

8:23

NASB
"will grasp the garment of a Jew"

NKJV
"will grasp the sleeve of a Jewish man"

NRSV
"shall take hold of a Jew, grasping his garment"

TEV
"come to one Jew"

"will take a Jew by the sleve"

JPSOA
"they will take hold of every Jew by a corner of his cloak"

Peshitta
"shall take hold of the skirt of a Jew"

NIV
"will take firm hold of one Jew by the hem of his robe"

The Hebrew VERB "take hold" (BDB 304, KB 302) in the Hiphil stem is
repeated twice (first IMPERFECT then PERFECT with waw) for emphasis
and urgency (see use in 1 Kgs. 1:50; 2:28; 2 Kgs. 4:27; Prov. 26:17; Isa. 4:1). In the ANE this was a gesture of submission
or supplication.

The intended purpose of the call of Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:3) is to be realized!

The confusion (many languages) of the tower of Babel has now been overcome. The beginning
of the church at Pentecost (cf. Acts 2) is the reversal of Genesis 10-11, as these people from many lands heard the
gospel in their own language. This verse is a prophetic glimpse.

8:8,10; 45:14) and the goal of creation (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8-9). This was what Israel was meant to convey to the nations!
The barrier (cf. Gen. 3:10-21) between Him and mankind is removed.

"God" is Elohim; see

This is a study guide commentary, which

paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- As I read and research this chapter, it again reminds me of the pain I feel for

- people who know God only through the Mosaic Covenant (i.e., national Israel)

- people who violate the Mosaic Covenant with terrible consequences (most of Israel's
history, Lev. 26; Deut. 28)

- the Gentile nations who remained in ignorance of God for so long

- This chapter is a powerful promise of restoration. It uses utopian language of a future day of
a secure and just society which includes all peoples.

- However, that society is centered by a faithful, repentant Israel with Jerusalem as its capital. This does not describe

- the post-exilic Judah

- the modern secular state of Israel

For a good discussion of the place of modern Israel in God's plan, see the YouTube video by Steve Gregg, "The Modern State of Israel."
I think it will make you rethink much that you have been told and assume to be true about Israel.

- Neither Jesus, nor His Apostles, ever asserts or affirms any OT promises to national Israel. Only believing Israel
(i.e., Rom. 2:28-29; 9-11) is included in NT promises and salvation.

- My love for the Bible and my trust in God's character cause me great confusion (cf. Isa. 55:6-13). Is the NT about Israel?

- As a follower of Christ I must assert and cling to the priority of the New Covenant. Jesus, not Israel (i.e., Matt. 5:17-19),
is the ultimate revelation of God (i.e., Matt. 5:21-48). The NT is about Jesus, not Israel!

- Jesus, Himself, said such harsh things to the Jews of His day (i.e., Matt. 12:34; 23:2-39; Luke 20:9-19). I have come to
believe the Olivet Discourse and the book of Revelation are about God's judgment on "those who pierced Him"
(cf. Rev. 1:7). For some good books on Preterism, see

- John Bray, Matthew 24 Fulfilled

- Kenneth Gentry

- Before Jerusalem Fell

- The Beast of Revelation

- The Apocalypse of John: A Preterist Commentary of the Book of Revelation

- Four Views on the Book of Revelation, several authors, note pp. 39-92

- Steve Gregg

- Revelation: Four views, Revised and Expanded

- Why Not Full-Preterism? A Partial-Preterist Response to a Novel Theological Innovation

- Many thought provoking YouTube videos on biblical issues and controversies; his website is www.thenarrowpath.com; I highly recommend this brother's Bible study and lectures on contemporary controversies.

- Gary DeMar

- Last Days Madness: Obsession of the Modern Church

- End Time Fiction" A Biblical Consideration of Left Behind Theology

- Bruce Gore, YouTube video, "The Apocalypse in Space and Time" (10 lectures with detailed historical and Early Church Father quotes; very detailed and interesting)

- So, I affirm that the Old Covenant has been fulfilled (Matt. 5:17-19). It is still inspired and relevant, but it has been
superseded (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; the book of Hebrews).
